item.description: llama-quant : fix 4D tensor quantization using ggml_nrows() and name-based expert detection (#30820) * llama-quant : fix quantizing 4D tensors nrows_total was ne[1]*ne[2], so for a 4D tensor only the first ne[2] slices were quantized and the rest of the rows were dropped. Use ggml_nrows(tensor) to count all rows, including ne[3]. Fixes #29916 * llama-quant : detect expert tensors by name and fix imatrix size for 4D tensors The MXFP4_MOE path used ne[2] > 1 to detect MoE expert tensors. This is wrong for non-expert tensors with 3 or more dims, e.g. MLA projections (BailingMoE3) and 4D conv kernels. Use the tensor name instead: all tensors used by GGML_OP_MUL_MAT_ID are named *_exps or *_chexps. This also removes the BailingMoE3 special case. The imatrix holds one vector of ne[0] values per 2D slice, so the expected size is ne[0]*ne[2]*ne[3], not ne[0]*ne[2]. This matches how the imatrix is indexed per row for 4D tensors in llama_tensor_quantize_impl. item.description: CUDA: fuse FFN gate/up matmuls and GLU in MMQ with interleaved gate/up rows (#29948) * cuda: fuse FFN gate/up and GLU in MMQ with interleaved gate/up rows For prompt processing, run the gate and up matmuls of a dense FFN as one mul_mat_q launch and apply the GLU in the write-back. - The loaders take the gate weights as a second pointer and fill the weight tile with up and gate rows interleaved in chunks of 8, so each thread holds an up value and the matching gate value (rows r and r + 8 of an MMA tile). - The MMA loop is unchanged: same tile, warp layout, vec_dot and one sum[] per thread. The fused write-back computes the GLU from registers and writes half the rows. - The fused path uses the regular tiling (no stream-k) with the column tiles innermost so that neighbouring blocks share weight tiles. - Enabled for Q4_K, Q5_K, Q6_K, Q8_0 and IQ4_XS on NVIDIA Turing and newer. * cuda: assert the fused MMQ gate argument and trim redundant comments * cuda: move the fused MMQ hint check to should_fuse and add TODOs * cuda: pass prec_src1 to the fused MMQ write-back * cuda: fuse only with efficient tiling and no fallback, merge the GLU write-back * cuda: require has_fusion explicitly, drop the fusion-only src1 precision check * cuda: launch the fused MMQ kernel through the stream-k kernel with one block per tile * cuda: inline the MMQ tiling-efficiency check * tests: one fused gate/up MMQ case per type and GLU op * cuda: always launch the fused MMQ kernel with one block per tile * tests: shorten the fused gate/up MMQ test comment * cuda: select the fused MMQ loader and write-back in ggml_cuda_mmq_get_util_funcs * cuda: run the fused MMQ kernel on the plain tiling path * cuda: put the column tiles innermost in the MMQ plain tiling path **Website:** - item.description: chat : reject JSON nested more than 128 levels before walking it (#30242) * chat : reject JSON nested more than 128 levels before walking it The schema builder, the jinja engine and the decision code walk request JSON with recursion. item.description: mtmd : lfm2 resize matches torchvision (#30943) * mtmd : lfm2 bilinear resize matches torchvision Lfm2VlImageProcessor and d1-omni vision.py resize uint8 images with torchvision (antialias=True). That is Pillow's algorithm, except that the weights are int16 with as many fractional bits as the largest weight allows, where Pillow uses 22 bits. The Pillow port was 1-2 levels off on about 1% of the values of the d1-omni and LFM2.5-VL crops. RESIZE_ALGO_BILINEAR_TORCH rounds the weights of the Pillow port to that precision and scales them back to 22 bits, which gives the output of torchvision with the same passes, and "bilinear" maps to it for LFM2 and d1-omni. item.description: hip: fix bf16 WMMA operand vector type for gfx11/gfx12 (#30885) The __builtin_amdgcn_wmma_f32_16x16x16_bf16_w32 (and _gfx12) builtins take their A/B operands as vectors of short (_ExtVector<16, short> / _ExtVector<8, short>), not __bf16. Declaring the fragments as ext_vector_type(N) __bf16 fails to compile: error: cannot initialize a parameter of type 'short __attribute__((ext_vector_type(16)))' with an lvalue of type 'const bf16x16_t' (vector of 16 '__bf16' values) short and __bf16 are both 16-bit and the value is only ever passed to the builtin via reinterpret_cast over raw bytes, so changing the element type is bit-identical. The operand type has been short since the builtin was introduced, so this works across LLVM/ROCm versions without a version gate. Fixes HIP builds for RDNA3 (gfx1150/1151) and RDNA4 (gfx1200/1201). item.description: llama: create new fused op for QSA mask (#30640) * llama: create new fused op for QSA scoring * enroll glm5.3-next too * tests : initialize the remaining tensors in test_kpool_mask The harness sentinels were left uninitialized, so leftover memory could read as NaN and fail the NaN check. * ggml: generalize the k-pool mask op into ggml_top_k_mask The k-pool mask op only covered the pooled QSA selection of qwen4exp and glm5-next, while the DSA models and the DeepSeek V4 CSA build the same top-k mask by hand with fill, set_rows and add. ggml_top_k_mask(mask, top_k, score, blocks, extra) keeps the mask cells of the live picks and the extra cells, and sets the rest to -inf. Every row tensor is 4D in the layout of top_k, and the mask is broadcast to those rows, so a selection can also be made per head. score, blocks and extra are optional: without score every pick is live, without blocks a pick is a cell, and extra holds the cells a row keeps without a pick. llm_graph_context::build_fused_top_k_mask views the row tensors in the layout of kq_mask and registers the fused node. item.description: server: add realtime transcription API (#30636) * server: add realtime transcription API * drop transcription_sessions * proxy ws * add docs * server: let the API key middleware guard the websocket httplib runs the pre-routing handler before the websocket upgrade, so the API key middleware answers 401 at handshake like any other route. This covers the router proxy, whose children run keyless, and accepts the same key forms as HTTP (Bearer, raw key, X-Api-Key). * server: keep realtime slots out of the prompt loop A realtime slot waiting for audio is GENERATING with nothing to decode, so it fell through the prompt loop and took slot_batched. A request on a higher slot then failed can_batch_with on the task type and starved for the whole session. Realtime slots have no prompt: the loop sets them up once and always leaves them. * server: start the realtime session once its slot is live The audio stream was created in the prompt loop, which skips a slot that cannot batch with the one generating, and session.created went out before the task was posted: early appends failed and the reader quit, leaving the socket open and the slot held until the HTTP timeout. The slot now sets up its stream at launch and signals it with the begin result, session.created waits for it, and a reader that stops closes the socket so the session ends with it. * server: name the committed item in input_audio_buffer.committed Per the Realtime spec, item_id is the item made from the committed audio and previous_item_id the one committed before it, null for the first. committed now comes before the transcript that completes that item, and both go out with the item switch under one lock, so a delta cannot land between them. * server: use the GA transcription session shape The session object follows the GA Realtime schema: type transcription, with the input format, transcription model, turn detection and noise reduction under audio.input. item.description: ggml-cpu : select the NEON fp32->fp16 conversion (#30505) The __ARM_NEON branch defines both GGML_CPU_COMPUTE_* macros but selects only FP16_TO_FP32, so FP32_TO_FP16 falls through to the portable software conversion while neon_compute_fp32_to_fp16, a single fcvt, stays defined and referenced by nothing. __POWER9_VECTOR__ and __riscv_zfhmin select both. Add an #error pair that refuses a branch defining a COMPUTE macro without selecting it. item.description: tests : make MoE router selection independent of the backend noise (#30818) * tests : make MoE router selection independent of the backend noise The router scores are in the range 0, 1), so a random draw can leave the last expert (or expert group) still selected and the first one dropped tied within the noise between the backends. They then route a token to different experts and the logits differ by 4e-3 instead of the usual 5e-7. Beam is the only arch here with a real top-k (8 experts, 2 used) and a group top-k (4 groups, 2 used), so it is the only one that hits this: 2 of 20 seeds failed on an M2 Ultra, the other MoE archs select 2 of 2 and cannot tie. Fill the selection bias with a ramp of step 2 to give every expert a score range of its own, which turns the top-k into a function of the expert index alone. The bias affects only the selection, the weights still come from the unbiased probs, so the MoE output keeps its magnitude. Beam now matches the CPU reference within 4e-7 for all of 160 seeds.
